rationale: I acted on the hypothesis that the PRESENT-80 cipher requires a final AddRoundKey step after the 31st round (using the key schedule output K32), which the previous design omitted — the previous version stopped after applying the permutation of round 31 without XORing the final whitening key. I added a `finalizing` state that performs this extra `state ^ key[79:16]` XOR before asserting `done`. If this repair also fails, I would next carefully verify the key schedule rotation direction and amount (the PRESENT spec rotates the 80-bit key register left by 61 bits, equivalent to `{k[18:0], k[79:19]}`), double-check which bits of the key are used for the round key (bits 79 down to 16, i.e., the top 64 bits), and also verify the round counter XOR position in the key schedule (bits 19:15 vs. 15:11) against the PRESENT specification, as an off-by-one in the key schedule XOR position is a common source of silent ciphertext mismatch.
